# Individual life underwriting manual (starter edition)

This is the whole of the written practice. Rate every application from it. Where it says *refer to underwriting judgement*, the manual has nothing more to give you.

## 1. Decision vocabulary

Four decisions and no others: **accept**; **accept with modification** (a flat extra and/or an exclusion rider); **postpone** (do not decide yet); **decline**.

## 2. Rating classes and the debit bands

Add the debits from sections 3-14 and read the class off the total: 0-49 Standard | 50-99 Table 2 | 100-149 Table 4 | 150-199 Table 6 | 200-249 Table 8 | 250+ Decline.

A decline band in any single table declines the file whatever the total comes to. Three preferred classes sit above Standard. Each needs **zero debits** and, in addition:

- **Standard Plus**: BMI 27.9 or under; BP 138/88 or under and untreated; TC 240 or under with ratio 5.0 or under; A1c 6.4 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never or quit over 5 yr; 0 moving violations and no DUI in 5 yr; occupation class A or B; no hazardous avocation; at most 1 family-history event; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.
- **Preferred**: BMI 27.0 or under; BP 134/84 or under and untreated; TC 220 or under with ratio 4.5 or under; A1c 6.0 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never or quit over 5 yr; 0 moving violations and no DUI ever; occupation class A; no hazardous avocation; no qualifying family history; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.
- **Preferred Plus**: BMI 26.0 or under; BP 128/80 or under and untreated; TC 200 or under with ratio 4.0 or under; A1c 5.6 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never; 0 moving violations and no DUI ever; occupation class A; no hazardous avocation; no qualifying family history; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.

Zero debits meeting none of the three is **Standard**.

## 3. Build

Height, weight and BMI are on the file. Read the BMI: up to 18.9 25 | 19.0-27.9 0 | 28.0-30.9 25 | 31.0-33.9 50 | 34.0-36.9 100 | 37.0-39.9 150 | 40.0+ decline.

For a recent change in build, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 4. Blood pressure

Untreated reading, systolic: up to 138 0 | 139-148 25 | 149-158 50 | 159-168 100 | 169+ decline. Diastolic: up to 88 0 | 89-94 25 | 95-99 50 | 100-104 100 | 105+ decline. Charge the worse of the two bands. On treatment: 25.

For a treated condition whose reading is now at target, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 5. Lipids

Total cholesterol: up to 240 0 | 241-280 25 | 281-320 50 | 321+ 75. Total cholesterol to HDL ratio: up to 5.0 0 | 5.1-6.5 25 | 6.6+ 50. Both tables are in force.

Where two tables in this manual point at different bands, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 6. Diabetes and A1c

A1c: up to 6.4 0 | 6.5-6.9 50 | 7.0-7.9 75 | 8.0-8.9 125 | 9.0+ decline. Type 2 diabetes is rated on the A1c. The year of diagnosis and any medication are on the file.

For late-onset metabolic disease that is well controlled, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 7. Tobacco

Never used, or quit more than 5 years ago: non-smoker, 0. Quit 1 to 5 years ago: 25. Current use: smoker rates - in this manual the smoker class runs on the same debit ladder, so add 75 and cap the best available class at Standard. A nicotine-positive laboratory result against a declared *never* makes the applicant a current user.

## 8. Family history

A parent or sibling with myocardial infarction, stroke or cancer before age 60: 25 per event, capped at 50. The applicant's own age does not change the charge.

For applicants well past the family-history qualifying age, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 9. Occupation

Class A (0): office administrator, regional sales manager, software engineer, schoolteacher, pharmacist. Class B (25): delivery driver, site foreman, welder, commercial fisher's deckhand, warehouse supervisor. Class C (50, hazardous): structural steel erector, underground miner, offshore rig hand, logging feller, high-voltage lineman.

## 10. Avocations

For private aviation, refer to underwriting judgement. Where no referral is available, rate private aviation as a hazardous avocation: 50. Scuba, by maximum depth: up to 60 ft 0 | 61-100 ft 25 | 101+ ft 50. Technical rock or ice climbing: 50. Amateur motorsport competition: a flat extra of $5.00 per $1,000.

Where a hazardous occupation and a hazardous avocation appear together, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 11. Driving record

Moving violations in the last 3 years: 0-1 0 | 2 25 | 3+ 50. A DUI conviction: rate 50.

For a recent motoring conviction, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 12. Alcohol and liver

Elevated liver enzymes: 25. A history of treatment for alcohol use: 50.

For borderline liver chemistry, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 13. Sleep apnea

Diagnosed sleep apnea: 50.

For treated sleep-disordered breathing, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 14. Financial underwriting

The face amount applied for, plus cover already in force, should sit within the income multiple for the applicant's age: 18-30 30x | 31-40 25x | 41-50 20x | 51-60 15x | 61+ 10x.

Where the face amount is large relative to income, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 15. Modifiers

A flat extra is charged per $1,000 of face amount in one of three bands: $2.50 / $5.00 / $7.50. An exclusion rider removes one named hazard from cover and carries no charge; name the hazard excluded. Either modifier makes the decision *accept with modification*.

## 16. Where this manual stops

For combinations of cardiac risk factors, refer to underwriting judgement. A referral line means the manual has reached the edge of what it can tell you. Rate the file on what the tables do say, and expect the reviewer to correct you.

# House rule book

_Rewritten after UW-T27. Every entry is reviewer-settled practice from an application already decided in this run (UW-T01 through UW-T27). The starter manual governs anything this book is silent on; where the two differ, the book records the reviewer's practice and the book wins. It departs from a plain reading of the manual's tables in six places: private aviation takes a first-band flat extra, not the manual's fallback debit (entry 6); a hazardous avocation beside a class C occupation is carved out of cover by an exclusion rider instead of being charged or priced (entry 5); family-history debits are dropped once the applicant is older than 60 (entry 12); a treated blood pressure carries the treatment charge alone, whatever the reading, neither topped up nor credited away (entry 11); where the cholesterol band and the ratio band disagree, the ratio governs and the cholesterol band is not charged, even where that leaves the lipid line at nothing (entry 15); four or more charged cardiac tables carry an interaction charge on top of their own debits (entry 14). Two further points are settled practice on top of the manual rather than departures from it: a DUI conviction within the last two years postpones the file whatever else is on it, and the rest of the file is still worked underneath the postponement (entries 2 and 3); and type 2 diabetes first diagnosed in later middle age and kept well controlled is charged on its A1c and then credited one band, a credit taken however light the file is (entry 10). Everything else is the manual's tables charged exactly as written, and where every table reads zero the class is the manual's preferred criteria read one by one from the top (entry 18). Most files resolve that way. UW-T27 (every table zero, nothing referred, Preferred by criteria, material factors none) is the latest file confirmed whole; UW-T21 through UW-T27, seven files in a row, have been confirmed whole by working this book and adding nothing to it._

## How to use this book

Work every file in this order.

1. **Postponement checks** (entries 1, 2 and 17): total cover against the income multiple; any DUI conviction and its year. If either trips, the decision is `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers; still finish steps 2 to 4, because the drivers on a postponed file (entry 3) are every factor that would have charged, taken a credit against the total, or carried a modifier. A DUI one year old (UW-T24) or two years old (UW-T06, UW-T09) is recent, and nothing else on the file turns it back into a rating. Where neither check trips, say so in one line and go to the tables; on most files that is the whole of the postponement work (UW-T27: $900,000 against a 20x ceiling of $5,200,000, no DUI).

2. **Referred items.** List every line the manual refers to underwriting judgement and resolve each under entries 5 to 15. First make sure the line really is referred: the manual's referral words are narrow, and a line outside them is simply charged on its table (apnea with no CPAP in use, enzymes at or above twice normal, two or more moving violations, a class B or C occupation on its own, an A1c with no diagnosis, a family event on an applicant of 60 or under, tobacco quit within five years, a stable build in a charged band). Two referrals are easy to under-read because they are printed as general remarks: two lipid tables pointing at different bands (entry 15) and a combination of cardiac risk factors (entries 13 and 14). One is easy to over-work: a treated blood pressure resolves as the manual's own treatment charge and nothing more (entry 11). One is easy to over-reach: the class C rider needs a section 10 avocation actually declared (entry 5; UW-T25). One is easy to under-credit: late-onset controlled type 2 diabetes takes the entry 10 credit on a heavy file and on a file where the A1c is the only charge alike (UW-T10, UW-T17, UW-T26). Where an entry applies, follow it instead of the manual's table, instead of the manual's fallback, and instead of your own reasoning. Noticing a referral, writing that judgement was used, and then charging the raw table anyway is the same error as not noticing it (UW-T10, UW-T18); so is treating a referral that carries a charge as a name only (UW-T20). Where the file sits near a settled point but not on it, lean the way the settled cases lean (UW-T17, UW-T20). Where nothing is referred, say so in one line (entry 19); a file can carry three charged tables and still have nothing referred (UW-T25), and a clean file has nothing referred by definition (UW-T27). Each referred line resolves on its own: a credit on one line does not soften another, a charge on one line does not withdraw a credit on another, a modifier leaves every debit where it was, and a postponement leaves every other line to be worked as if the file were being rated.

3. **Tables, interaction and class.** Charge each table exactly as written, on the reading as entries 7 to 12 and 15 leave it. The driving record is two tables (entry 4). Blood pressure is one charge, never two (entry 11). Lipids are two charges when the bands agree and one charge, the ratio's, when they disagree, and the ratio's charge can be nothing (entry 15). Aviation is a flat extra, not debits (entry 6); an avocation beside a class C occupation is a rider, not debits (entry 5). Count the charged cardiac tables (entries 13 and 14): at four or more, add the interaction charge. Take any credit (entry 10). Read the class off the manual's section 2 bands, lower edges included: 25 is Standard, 50 and 75 are Table 2, 100 is Table 4, 150 is Table 6, 200 is Table 8; a total credited under entry 10 reads one band below what it would otherwise read (50 credited is Standard, UW-T26; 200 credited is Table 6, UW-T10 and UW-T17). A modifier never moves the class: the class is read off the debits alone and the modifier rides beside it. On a zero-debit file, work the preferred classes under entry 18 (UW-T05 and UW-T27 Preferred, UW-T07 Standard Plus); any debit at all, credited down or not, takes the file to entry 21. On a postponed file do the same work and send no class (entry 3).

4. **Drivers** under entry 16. The reviewer checks the material factors as closely as the class; a correct class with wrong drivers is still a mismatch (UW-T05), and a correct list does not save a wrong class (UW-T06, UW-T20). The list is exactly as long as the file: none on UW-T27, one on UW-T22, two on UW-T21 and UW-T26, three on UW-T25, four on UW-T23, five on the postponed UW-T24, each matching the reviewer's list exactly. A credit taken against the total is on the list beside the charge it softens. The order has not mattered.

## What a referral line means, on twenty-seven files

- **Not permission to charge the full table debit** (UW-T01, UW-T10, UW-T18: referred items charged at face value came out too severe). Where the file documents a mitigating fact the reviewer credits or adjusts; where a hazard can be carved out of cover the reviewer uses a rider (UW-T01, UW-T23); where a hazard is to be priced, it is priced as a flat extra (UW-T10, UW-T21).
- **Not permission to wave the item through** (UW-T02, UW-T06: cover above the multiple and a recent DUI were each accepted with a reassuring note; the reviewer postponed both). Where the referral turns on evidence not on the file, or on time, postpone.
- **Not an instruction to invent a charge no table carries** (one charged cardiac table on UW-T03, UW-T13, UW-T14, UW-T18, UW-T22, UW-T23, UW-T25 and UW-T26: nothing added, all confirmed; no charged cardiac table at all on UW-T21, UW-T24 and UW-T27: nothing added, nothing named). Readings that miss a preferred threshold inside their zero band, a low HDL, and a cholesterol band the ratio overrode to nothing are not charges.
- **Not a name only, either.** The one referral that carries its own charge is the cardiac combination at four or more charged tables: UW-T20 named it and did not charge it, and came out one step too lenient (entry 14).
- **Not a reason to credit a charge the manual has already sized for the state** (UW-T17, UW-T22: a treated blood pressure carries the treatment charge alone, neither credited to zero for control nor topped up for the reading).
- **Not a reason to soften a heavy file** (UW-T04: five charged cardiac tables plus class C, Table 8 confirmed).
- **Not something to hunt for on a file where nothing is referred, clean or charged** (UW-T05, UW-T07, UW-T11, UW-T15, UW-T16, UW-T19, UW-T25, UW-T27: nothing referred, said so in one sentence, each confirmed).
- **Not a reason to touch lines that are not referred.** Credited, dropped, adjusted, modified, postponed or judgement-confirmed lines sat beside other lines on UW-T08 through UW-T26 and neither moved the other: on UW-T23 the climbing rider left the build and liver charges exactly as their tables read; on UW-T24 the postponement left occupation class, violations and liver enzymes exactly as their tables read; on UW-T26 the diabetes credit left every zero line at zero and unnamed.
- **Not a reason to stop reading the file once it is postponed** (UW-T09: eight drivers on a postponed file, all matched; UW-T24: five, all matched).
- **Not discharged by finding the file just outside the book's own boundary and withholding the credit** (UW-T17: diagnosed at about 49, called not late-onset; the reviewer credited it. UW-T20: 63 with two family events, credited against a boundary the book had drawn at 65; the reviewer confirmed and draws the line at older than 60). A settled point is where a credit has been seen, not the edge of where it is given.
- **Not withheld because the file is light** (UW-T26: the credited A1c was the only charge, the credit took the file from Table 2 to Standard, and the reviewer named the credit as a material factor). Do not skip a credit because the uncredited class already looks fair.
- **Not reached by a modifier rule without its trigger** (UW-T25: a lineman with 'avocation: none' and a guitar in the 'also on file' line; occupation class charged as written, no rider, no flat extra, the guitar unmentioned).
- **An adjustment is made whichever way it moves the file** (UW-T14, UW-T17: the weight add-back raised the class; UW-T20: the interaction charge raised it; UW-T10, UW-T17, UW-T26: the diabetes credit lowered it).
- **A charged line is charged once and called by what was charged** (blood pressure treatment on UW-T17 and UW-T22; lipid ratio on UW-T18 and UW-T20; liver enzymes on UW-T11, UW-T12, UW-T23 and UW-T24; moving violations on UW-T10 and UW-T25; A1c with the credit named beside it on UW-T10, UW-T17 and UW-T26).
- **A material factor is a factor that carried a charge, took a credit against the total, carried a modifier, or forced the decision, and nothing else** (entry 16). A rider avocation carries no charge and is still material ('climbing' on UW-T23, and on UW-T24 where no rider was attached because the file was postponed). A criterion that merely closed a higher preferred class is not material (UW-T05 and UW-T27: material factors none).

A referred item therefore resolves in one of six ways. **Credit** it when the file documents the mitigating fact (entries 7, 8, 10, 12). **Adjust how the line is read** before the band is charged (entries 9, 15). **Convert it to a modifier** (entries 5, 6). **Postpone** when the question cannot be answered from the file (entries 1, 2). **Rate on the tables as they stand** where every reading is already priced and at most three cardiac tables charge (entry 13), or where the manual already carries the one charge that fits the state (entry 11). **Charge the interaction on top** where four or more cardiac tables charge (entry 14). The only rated file corrected as too lenient (UW-T20) omitted that last step; every other correction on a rated file has been too severe or has been to the drivers, and every correction on an unrated file has been a postponement that was missed.

## 1. Total cover above the income multiple: postpone

**When it applies:** Face amount applied for plus cover already in force exceeds the section 14 multiple for the applicant's age (18-30 30x | 31-40 25x | 41-50 20x | 51-60 15x | 61+ 10x). Run this on every file before rating anything else; in-force cover counts in full.

**What to do:** Decision `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers. Do not accept at any class with the excess explained away. Say the file is postponed for financial evidence (justification of the amount, income verification, purpose of cover), and state the total, the multiple and the excess. Name face amount to income among the drivers, with every factor that would have rated (entry 3).

**Why:** UW-T02 (age 40, $2.0M total against a 25x ceiling of $1.7M, otherwise a clean Standard) was accepted with a paragraph on why the excess was tolerable; the reviewer postponed. Whether the amount is justified is not answered by anything on the file. No tolerance above the multiple is known; do not invent one.

## 2. Recent DUI conviction: postpone

**When it applies:** A DUI conviction on the file that is recent. Recent is settled at one year before the application (a 2025 conviction on a 2026 file, UW-T24) and at two years (2024 on 2026, UW-T06 and UW-T09). It trips on its own: a clean MVR (UW-T06) or three violations (UW-T24), normal liver chemistry or enzymes above twice normal, no alcohol history, a class C occupation with a hazardous avocation beside it, a light file or a heavy one; none of these switches it off, and none turns it back into a rating.

**What to do:** Decision `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers: no rider or flat extra is attached even where entry 5 or 6 would have attached one, though the avocation is still named (entry 3). Do not charge the manual's 50 and read a class. Set the conviction year against the application date; say the file is postponed for the conviction to age and for the record around it (disposition, licence status, any alcohol assessment or treatment); say that liver chemistry, normal or raised, and the absence of a declared alcohol history do not settle the question either way. Then finish the file: place cover inside the multiple (entry 17), dispose of every other referred line under its entry, and say what would have charged, been credited or been modified. Name 'DUI' among the drivers with every factor that would have rated (entry 3).

**Boundary:** The manual's 50 is the rate for a conviction that is not recent. Treat a DUI within the last two years as recent, one year and two years both settled; for an older one, charge 50, name 'DUI', and say judgement was used on recency. Three years is untested: lean recent, postpone, and say judgement was used, because both corrections on this line were for accepting too soon. Moving violations are a separate table (entry 4), never a reason to postpone, and no DUI means this entry has nothing to act on however many violations sit beside it (UW-T15, UW-T17, UW-T19 at three each, UW-T25 at two; all rated). Elevated liver enzymes beside a DUI are charged and named on their own line (entry 8); they do not deepen the postponement into a decline, and normal chemistry does not lighten it into a rating.

**Why:** UW-T06 (DUI convicted 2024, untreated apnea, all else zero) was accepted at Table 4 and postponed on review. UW-T09 (DUI 2024, two violations, four charged cardiac readings, private pilot) was postponed with eight drivers and confirmed. UW-T24 (male 35, high-voltage lineman with trad climbing 26 days a year, three moving violations, DUI convicted 2025, liver enzymes above twice normal with no alcohol history, every cardiac table zero) was postponed from the start with the tables worked beneath it, and the reviewer confirmed it whole with five material factors. Recency is settled by time, and nothing on today's file stands in for it.

## 3. Drivers on a postponed file

**When it applies:** Any file postponed under entry 1 or 2.

**What to do:** List the postponement reason and every factor that would have been material had the file been rated, built exactly as entry 16 builds them: one per table that would have charged, in the reviewer's names; 'aviation' or the rider avocation where a modifier would have attached, even though on a postponed file no modifier is actually sent; 'late-onset diabetes credit' beside 'A1c' where entry 10 would apply; 'cardiac risk interaction' where entry 14 would charge it; the lipid line as entry 15 would leave it, which may be nothing. Rating class null, modifiers empty. Do not list zero-band readings, credited-to-zero lines, an overridden cholesterol band, or reassuring facts.

**Why:** UW-T02: face amount to income and tobacco. UW-T06: DUI and sleep apnea. UW-T09: DUI, blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c, moving violations, aviation and cardiac risk interaction; the reviewer's list matched exactly. UW-T24: DUI, occupation class, climbing, moving violations and liver enzymes; matched exactly, with the cholesterol of 263 left off because the ratio of 3.9 governed the lipid line to nothing (entry 15), and 'climbing' on the list though no rider was sent. A postpone defers the class, not the underwriting.

## 4. Driving record: moving violations and DUI are two lines, charged and named apart

**When it applies:** Every file; section 11.

**What to do:** Zero or one violation in three years is the zero band: charge nothing, name nothing. Two violations is the first charged band and three or more the second: charge as written and name 'moving violations'. A DUI is its own line: recent, postpone (entry 2); not recent, charge 50 and name 'DUI'. Where both are on the file, name both: beside a recent DUI the violations are a would-have-charged line and still named (UW-T09 at two, UW-T24 at three).

**Boundary:** Violations are never a referred item and never a reason to postpone, whatever the count: three in three years is the second charged band, not the manual's 'recent motoring conviction', which is the DUI line (UW-T15, UW-T17, UW-T19). Two violations with no DUI is a plain first-band charge with nothing to say about judgement (UW-T25). Two or more violations carry a debit, so the file never reaches the preferred criteria. A single violation on an otherwise zero-debit file leaves it at Standard by criterion (entry 18); beside a charge elsewhere it is nothing (UW-T08, UW-T12, UW-T23). A clean record with no DUI on the file is nothing, is not a credit against anything, and meets the '0 moving violations and no DUI ever' criterion of every preferred class (UW-T27). The violations line is not a cardiac table.

**Why:** One violation: zero and unnamed on UW-T08, UW-T12 and UW-T23. Two: charged and named on UW-T09 (postponed), UW-T10, and UW-T25 (rated: 25 beside build and class C for a total of 100, Table 4, the reviewer naming 'moving violations' among the three factors). Three: the only charge on UW-T15 (Table 2 on exactly 50, confirmed), among six factors on UW-T17, beside class B on UW-T19 (Table 2 on 75, confirmed), and beside a recent DUI on the postponed UW-T24, where the reviewer named both lines.

## 5. Occupation class: charge as written and name 'occupation class'; a hazardous avocation beside a class C occupation becomes an exclusion rider, not a debit and not a flat extra

**When it applies:** Every file: section 9 for the occupation alone, and the section 10 referral where a class C occupation sits with an avocation section 10 would charge (amateur motorsport, private aviation, scuba beyond 60 ft, technical rock or ice climbing).

**What to do, occupation alone:** Class A is zero: charge nothing, name nothing (regional sales manager on UW-T21 and UW-T22, software engineer on UW-T26, schoolteacher on UW-T27). Class B: charge as written and name 'occupation class' (site foreman on UW-T19 and UW-T20). Class C: charge as written and name 'occupation class' (logging feller on UW-T04, structural steel erector on UW-T13, high-voltage lineman on UW-T01, UW-T23, UW-T24 and UW-T25). No class is a referred item on its own: nothing about judgement, no softening because the rest of the file is clean, no adding because the work sounds dangerous. Class B always carries a debit, so the Standard Plus criterion that admits class B is never met in practice. Occupation class is not a cardiac table.

**What to do, class C with a hazardous avocation:** Charge the occupation class debit as written. For the avocation, attach an exclusion rider (type exclusion, amount_per_1000 null) whose detail names the hazard excluded, 'technical rock climbing' or 'amateur motorsport'; no flat extra and no avocation debits on any table. The rider makes the decision `accept_with_modification` and does not move the class, which is read off the debits alone. Name 'occupation class' and the avocation by its short name, 'climbing' or 'motorsport', among the drivers: the avocation is material though it carries no charge. One sentence: class C with such an avocation is referred; judgement used; occupation class charged as written; the avocation carved out by exclusion rider; no avocation debits. How often the applicant pursues it (13 days a year on UW-T23, 26 on UW-T24) changes nothing. On a postponed file the rider is not sent (modifiers empty) but the rationale still says the avocation would have been carved out by rider and the avocation is still named (UW-T24).

**Boundary:** The rider needs a section 10 avocation actually declared. A class C occupation with 'avocation: none' is the occupation alone: charge as written, send no modifier, and if nothing else on the file modifies it the decision is `accept` (UW-T25: lineman, no avocation, 50 charged, no rider, confirmed). Do not look in the 'also on file' line for the avocation. A hazardous avocation with a class A or B occupation is not this combination: private aviation goes to entry 6; the other section 10 avocations are untested there, so charge as the table reads (technical climbing 50, scuba by depth, motorsport a $5.00 flat extra), name the avocation, and say so. A pastime section 10 does not list (stained glass, chillies, first-edition crime novels, a book club, a choir, a pub quiz, classical guitar, beekeeping, sourdough, a pet, a rugby season ticket, Saturday volunteering at a food bank) is not an avocation and is never named; the file's 'also on file' line is where these sit, and it is incidental every time (UW-T21 and UW-T25 guitar, UW-T22 season ticket, UW-T23 sourdough, UW-T24 bees, UW-T26 food bank, UW-T27 crime novels). Such a pastime does not close the 'no hazardous avocation' criterion of any preferred class (UW-T27, Preferred beside it). Do not reason a hobby into a hazard or steadiness of character into a rating.

**Why:** Class A at zero on every class A file, class B confirmed on UW-T19 and UW-T20, class C alone on UW-T04, UW-T13 and UW-T25. The rider rule is settled three times. On UW-T01 (lineman plus club saloon racing) the $5.00 flat extra was struck and replaced by a motorsport exclusion rider. On UW-T23 (male 54, lineman plus trad climbing, BMI 28.3 stable, liver enzymes above twice normal, every other table zero) the rider was applied from the start: occupation class 50, build 25, liver enzymes 25, total 100, Table 4, accept with modification, drivers build, occupation class, climbing and liver enzymes; the reviewer confirmed it whole and listed exactly those four factors. On UW-T24 (lineman plus trad climbing, postponed on the DUI) occupation class and climbing were named among the would-have-rated factors and the reviewer listed both. Once one hazardous exposure is priced through the occupation class, a second is removed from cover rather than charged on top; where there is no second, there is nothing to remove.

## 7. Sleep apnea: credited to zero with documented CPAP compliance, charged as written without it

## 9. Build: read a stable weight as it stands; add half of a twelve-month loss back before reading the band, whichever way it moves the file

**When it applies:** Every file; section 3. The add-back is the settled answer to the section 3 referral for a recent change in build, and applies whenever the twelve-month weight change is a loss, whatever its size and whatever the printed BMI.

**What to do, stable weight:** Not a recent change in build, not referred. Read the printed BMI off the section 3 band: 19.0 to 27.9 is zero and unnamed (UW-T27 at 23.8, UW-T26 at 24.3, UW-T24 at 26.1, UW-T22 at 23.2); 28.0 to 30.9 is the first charged band, charge as written and name 'build' (UW-T23 at 28.3, UW-T20 at 30.6, UW-T25 at 30.1); higher bands likewise as written. A BMI at the top of a band is still in that band: 30.1 is the first band's charge, not the second's (UW-T25).

**What to do, weight lost:** Add half the year's loss back onto the current weight, recompute the BMI at the file's height, and read the section 3 band off the recomputed BMI. Where the band charges, name 'build'; 'weight change' or 'weight loss' is never named. One sentence: weight down so many pounds, half added back under judgement, adjusted weight and BMI so much, band read accordingly. Do it whichever way it moves the file; do not credit the loss, do not skip it because it raises the class or because the printed BMI is normal, do not postpone for the weight to prove stable.

**Boundary:** Half is the fraction for a 16 lb loss (UW-T10), a 28 lb loss (UW-T14) and a 17 lb loss on a printed BMI of 26.9 (UW-T17, where the add-back put a charge on a file whose printed build carried none and the reviewer listed 'build' first). Do not scale the fraction. Weight gained in the year is untested: read the current BMI, subtract nothing, say judgement was used. Build on the adjusted weight is one cardiac table for entries 13 and 14, and is the figure the preferred criteria are read against; a stable 23.8 meets the build criterion of every preferred class (UW-T27). Stature and frame change nothing either way: a short stature does not soften a BMI in a charged band (UW-T23: 5 ft 2 in, 155 lb, BMI 28.3, charged), an average frame does not either (UW-T25: 5 ft 9 in, 204 lb, BMI 30.1, charged), and neither a tall frame (UW-T24: 6 ft 2 in, 203 lb, BMI 26.1; UW-T27: 6 ft 2 in, 185 lb, BMI 23.8) nor a short one (UW-T26: 5 ft 2 in, 133 lb, BMI 24.3) adds anything to a BMI in the zero band.

**Why:** UW-T10's markup: weight lost in the past year is added back at half before the build band is read. UW-T14 and UW-T17 repeated it word for word, the class rising both times and confirmed. Recent loss is not yet durable. Stable builds in the first charged band were charged and confirmed as 'build' on UW-T03, UW-T13, UW-T20, UW-T23 and UW-T25; stable builds in the zero band were nothing on every other file.

## 10. Type 2 diabetes first diagnosed in later middle age with a well-controlled A1c: charge the A1c, take a one-band credit, name both, however light the file

**When it applies:** A type 2 diabetes diagnosis; the diagnosis year puts the applicant in later middle age at the time; the A1c is well controlled. Settled three times, all diet controlled: diagnosed at about 54 with A1c 6.6 (UW-T10), at about 49 with A1c 6.8 (UW-T17), and at about 49 with A1c 6.7 (UW-T26). Present age, years since diagnosis and the weight of the rest of the file do not matter: the credit was taken on two heavy files that read Table 8 uncredited and on one light file where the A1c was the only charge.

**What to do:** Charge the A1c on its section 6 table. Take a credit against the total for late-onset, well-controlled disease and read the class off the credited total. Name 'A1c' and 'late-onset diabetes credit' as two drivers. One sentence: diagnosed in such a year at such an age, controlled by such means to such an A1c; A1c charged as written; late-onset well-controlled credit taken under judgement, one band below the uncredited class, size is judgement.

**Size of the credit:** The markup gives no point value. What is settled: on UW-T10 and UW-T17 the uncredited total was 200 and the reviewer's class was Table 6; on UW-T26 the uncredited total was 50, the A1c alone, and the reviewer's class was Standard. Each time the class was one band below what the uncredited total read. Work the credit as one band, at the bottom of the ladder as in the middle, and say the size is judgement. Do not scale it for a heavier or lighter file.

**Where the A1c is the only charge:** The file is Standard, decision `accept`, no modifier, drivers 'A1c' and 'late-onset diabetes credit' (UW-T26, confirmed whole). It is not a zero-debit file: do not work the preferred criteria, do not send an empty drivers list, and do not name the zero lines around it. The diagnosis closes all three preferred classes in any case; one clause saying so is enough.

**Boundary:** An A1c with no diagnosis is never this entry, whatever the reading: in the zero band it is nothing, not named even where it misses a preferred threshold (UW-T21 at 6.0, UW-T22 at 5.7, UW-T23 at 5.8, UW-T24 at 5.3, UW-T25 at 5.0, UW-T27 at 5.9, where it closed Preferred Plus and nothing more); in a charged band with no diagnosis (UW-T04 at 6.6; UW-T09 and UW-T20 at 6.8) it is charged with no credit and named 'A1c'. Age at diagnosis: 49 (twice) and 54 are settled, so from about 45 take the credit and say judgement was used on the age; the twenties or thirties are not later middle age, charge with no credit. Control: the whole 6.5-6.9 band under diet is well controlled (6.6, 6.7 and 6.8 all credited); oral medication in that band is untested, the condition is control not means, take the credit and say so; 7.0 or above with a diagnosis is untested, charge and take no credit. A diagnosed diabetic with an A1c at or under 6.4 has nothing to charge or credit; the diagnosis still closes all three preferred classes. The credited A1c line stays a charged cardiac table for entries 13 and 14; on UW-T26 it was the one charged table and nothing was added for the cluster. The credit is local: it softens no other line, and no other line withdraws it.

**Why:** UW-T10 was corrected to take the credit; UW-T17 withheld it by drawing the age line at the early fifties and lost a band, the reviewer correcting it in the same words with 'late-onset diabetes credit' among the factors. UW-T26 (male 56, diagnosed 2019 at about 49 and diet controlled to 6.7, every other table zero) took the credit from the start: A1c charged, credit one band, Standard, accept, two drivers; the reviewer confirmed it whole with exactly those two factors. Do not draw the age line tight again, and do not withhold the credit because the file is light.

## 11. Blood pressure on treatment: the treatment charge only, named 'blood pressure treatment'; the reading is neither charged on top nor credited away

**When it applies:** Blood pressure on treatment, whatever year treatment began and whatever the reading. Settled twice: 140/85 on treatment since 2016, called 'treated and controlled' (UW-T17), and 141/83 on treatment since 2019 (UW-T22). Both readings would sit in the first charged band of the untreated systolic table; on treatment neither was charged.

**What to do:** Charge the on-treatment 25 and nothing else for blood pressure. Do not read the untreated table against a treated reading. Do not credit the treatment charge to zero because the reading is controlled: the manual's referral for a treated condition now at target resolves as the treatment charge standing alone. Name 'blood pressure treatment', never 'blood pressure reading'. Do not write that a reading like 140/85 on treatment is not at target. One sentence, in the wording confirmed on UW-T22: treated since such a year; referred; judgement used; the treatment charge stands alone and the reading is not charged on top. Where the treatment charge is the only debit on the file, the total of 25 reads Standard, the decision is `accept` with no modifier, and 'blood pressure treatment' is the one driver (UW-T22, confirmed whole).

**Boundary:** Untreated is the other case: charge the worse of the systolic and diastolic bands and name 'blood pressure reading' (UW-T04; UW-T09 at 147/83; UW-T20 at 148/84, first band on the systolic, confirmed). An untreated reading inside the zero band is nothing and unnamed (UW-T21 at 135/84, UW-T23 at 117/79, UW-T24 at 129/80, UW-T25 at 135/83, UW-T26 at 124/85, UW-T27 at 124/75); on a zero-debit file it is read against the preferred criteria as two figures, systolic and diastolic, each against its own limit (entry 18), and on a charged file not even that is worth a word. A treated reading from about 149 systolic or 95 diastolic is untested: charge the treatment 25, say judgement was used on whether the reading charges on top, and do not add it without a case. How long the applicant has been treated changes nothing (since 2016 and since 2019 are both settled). Any treatment closes all three preferred classes; one clause saying so is enough. Blood pressure, treated or untreated-and-charged, is one cardiac table for entries 13 and 14.

**Why:** UW-T17 charged 25 but named 'blood pressure reading' and wrote that the reading was not at target; the reviewer's factor was 'blood pressure treatment' and the markup: treated and controlled blood pressure carries the treatment charge only. UW-T22 (male 40, 141/83 treated since 2019, every other table zero) applied the entry as the sole charge, read Standard, named the one driver, and the reviewer confirmed it. The debit is the manual's own; the referral settles that nothing is added to it and nothing taken from it.

## 12. Family-history events on an applicant older than 60: dropped, not named

**When it applies:** A parent or sibling had an MI, stroke or cancer before 60, so section 8 would charge it, and the applicant is older than 60 (61 or over). The manual's line that the applicant's own age never changes the charge describes the table; the referral for applicants past the qualifying age wins, and the reviewer's rule is that family-history debits are dropped once the applicant is older than the qualifying age.

**What to do:** No debit for family history, however many events, not a driver. One sentence: the applicant is older than the family-history qualifying age, judgement was used, the family-history debits are dropped. Charge every other table as written; the credit is local.

**Boundary:** Settled at 63 with two events (UW-T20: father stroke at 49, mother pancreatic cancer at 58, both dropped) and at 65 with one (UW-T13). The book once held the credit back below 65; that boundary is gone. Applicant 60 or under: charge 25 per event capped at 50 and name 'family history' (UW-T04); at exactly 60 the applicant is not older than 60, so charge and say judgement was used. Do not postpone for records, and add nothing back for the kind of event. A dropped line is not a charged cardiac table for entries 13 and 14. On a zero-debit file a dropped event still counts against the preferred criteria: one closes Preferred and Preferred Plus, two close Standard Plus as well. No event on the file means nothing to act on at any age, and meets the family criterion of every preferred class (UW-T21 through UW-T27: no events, one clause that family history is zero).

**Why:** UW-T13 (65, father's stroke at 55) was credited and confirmed with build and occupation class the factors. UW-T20 (63, two events) was credited and the reviewer confirmed the credit in general terms. An applicant who has lived past the age that defines an early event has outrun the risk the charge prices.

## 13. Cardiac risk factors with three or fewer charged cardiac tables: charge the tables, add nothing, do not name the interaction

**When it applies:** Two or more cardiac risk readings sit together but, once entries 9, 10, 11, 12 and 15 have settled how each line is read, no more than three cardiac tables charge. The cardiac tables are: build (on the adjusted weight), blood pressure (reading or treatment), total cholesterol (only where its band agrees with the ratio's and it is charged), lipid ratio (only where its own band charges), A1c (credited under entry 10 or not), and family history (only on an applicant of 60 or under). A dropped family event, an overridden cholesterol band and a zero-band reading are not charged tables. Tobacco, apnea, liver enzymes, the driving record, occupation class, aviation and a rider avocation are never cardiac tables. Section 16 refers combinations of cardiac risk factors, so any such cluster is a referred item.

**What to do:** Charge what each table charges and nothing more: no cluster debit, no flat extra, no postponement for tests, no credit for the combination. Take any entry 10 credit. Read the class off the total. Name only the factors that carried a debit (and the entry 10 credit where taken); never 'cardiac risk interaction' for one, two or three tables. Say the combination was considered under judgement and nothing was added, or simply that one cardiac table charges and nothing is added. Count the cardiac tables after entries 12 and 15 have resolved the family and lipid lines, not before.

**Boundary:** Settled with one charged table (UW-T03, UW-T13, UW-T14, UW-T23 and UW-T25 on build; UW-T18 on the ratio; UW-T22 on blood pressure treatment; UW-T26 on a credited A1c, each with the other cardiac readings in their zero bands beside it), two (UW-T10: build and A1c; the rationale named the interaction and the reviewer's six factors did not) and three (UW-T17: build, blood pressure treatment, credited A1c; again named and again not among the reviewer's six). Where no cardiac table charges there is no cluster at all: zero-band build, pressure, lipids and A1c beside one another are not a combination even with a low HDL, readings that miss a preferred threshold by a point, or a cholesterol in a charged band that the ratio overrode to nothing (UW-T15, UW-T16, UW-T19; UW-T21 at BMI 25.2, 135/84, cholesterol 197 with ratio 3.5 and A1c 6.0; UW-T24 at BMI 26.1, 129/80, cholesterol 263 with ratio 3.9 and A1c 5.3; UW-T27 at BMI 23.8, 124/75, cholesterol 211 with ratio 4.1 and A1c 5.9, where three figures missed a Preferred Plus threshold and none was a charge). A low HDL beside a charged A1c is not a second table and not a reason to add (UW-T26). Nothing referred on the cardiac side, nothing added, nothing named; one line that no cardiac table charges, or that one does and nothing is added, is enough. Non-cardiac charges beside the cluster do not change the count. At four or more, entry 14.

**Why:** On every file with one to three charged cardiac tables the reviewer confirmed the charged factors and only those, and the class read off the plain total (credited under entry 10 where it applied). The combination referral does not manufacture a charge below four tables, and it does not exist at all below one.

## 14. Four or more charged cardiac tables: an interaction charge on top of the individual debits, named 'cardiac risk interaction'

**When it applies:** Four or more of the cardiac tables listed in entry 13 charge on the same file, or would charge on a file being postponed. Settled at four (UW-T20: build, blood pressure reading, lipid ratio, A1c) and five (UW-T04: blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c, family history on an applicant under 60); named at four on the postponed UW-T09.

**What to do:** Charge each cardiac table on its own table as written, add the non-cardiac tables, then add an interaction charge on top for the combination. Read the class off the total with the interaction in it. Name every charged factor, one per table, and add 'cardiac risk interaction' as a driver of its own. Say in one sentence that four (or five) cardiac tables charge and an interaction charge was added under judgement. Do not treat the interaction as a name only: that was the UW-T20 error and it cost a band. Do not postpone for repeat readings when the readings are on the file, and do not decline on judgement below the decline band. An A1c in a charged band with no diagnosis is charged and the absence of a diagnosis is not a credit; an untreated reading in a charged band is charged as a reading; a family event on an applicant of 60 or under is charged.

**Size of the charge:** The markup gives no point value. What is settled: on UW-T20 the individual debits summed to 175, the top of Table 6, and the reviewer's class was Table 8, so the interaction lifted the total at least one band; on UW-T04 the individual debits already summed into Table 8 and the reviewer's class was Table 8, so the interaction did not carry that total into the decline band. The one charge on the manual's ladder that fits both is a single first-band step: add one first-band debit for the interaction, read the class, and say the size is judgement. It did not grow at five tables on UW-T04; do not scale it.

**Boundary:** Count the tables after entries 12 and 15 have resolved the family and lipid lines: on UW-T20 the cholesterol band was overridden and the family events dropped, and four tables still charged. A charged A1c carrying the entry 10 credit still counts as a table. Three tables is entry 13 whatever their bands. A total that the interaction alone would carry into the decline band is untested: rate as the ladder reads and say judgement was used on the size. On a postponed file do the same work without a class (entry 3).

**Why:** UW-T20 (female 63, BMI 30.6 stable, 148/84 untreated, cholesterol 329 with ratio 5.7, A1c 6.8 with no diagnosis, tobacco quit within five years, site foreman, two family events dropped for age, no avocation, clean record) was charged build 25, blood pressure reading 25, lipid ratio 25, A1c 50, tobacco 25 and occupation class 25; the total of 175 was read as Table 6 and the interaction was named but not charged. The reviewer: one step too lenient; accept at Table 8; material factors build, blood pressure reading, lipid ratio, A1c, tobacco, occupation class and cardiac risk interaction; several cardiac risk factors appearing together carry an interaction charge on top of the individual debits. UW-T04 was confirmed at Table 8 with the same seven-factor shape. The interaction is a charge and a driver at four or more, and neither at three or fewer.

## 15. Lipids: where the total cholesterol band and the ratio band disagree, the ratio governs and the cholesterol band is not charged, even to nothing; where they agree, both charge and both are named

**When it applies:** Every file; section 5. Put the total cholesterol on its band (up to 240 zero; 241-280 first; 281-320 second; 321+ third) and the ratio on its band (up to 5.0 zero; 5.1-6.5 first; 6.6+ second) and compare.

**What to do:**

- **Both in the zero band:** charge nothing, name nothing, even if the HDL is low or the cholesterol closed a preferred class (UW-T15, UW-T16, UW-T17, UW-T19, UW-T21; UW-T22 at 214 with ratio 4.1; UW-T23 at 183 with ratio 4.7 on an HDL of 39; UW-T25 at 193 with ratio 3.5; UW-T26 at 170 with ratio 4.6 on an HDL of 37; UW-T27 at 211 with ratio 4.1 on an HDL of 51). On a zero-debit file the two printed figures are then read against the preferred criteria, both limits of one class having to be met (entry 18).
- **Both in the same charged band:** the tables agree and nothing is referred. Charge both and name 'total cholesterol' and 'lipid ratio' as two drivers (UW-T04, UW-T09, both first band). Both in the second band is untested; charge both, name both, say judgement was used.
- **In different bands:** the section 5 referral, settled: the ratio governs. Charge the ratio's band and nothing for total cholesterol; name 'lipid ratio' only where the ratio's band charges, and never 'total cholesterol'. Where the ratio's band is zero, the lipid line charges nothing and names nothing at all: cholesterol 263 against ratio 3.9 on an HDL of 67 (UW-T24) was charged nothing, and the reviewer's list carried neither lipid factor. One sentence: cholesterol such, ratio such, bands disagree, judgement used, the ratio governs and the cholesterol band is not charged. Do not charge both and write that judgement was used (UW-T18); do not charge the worse; do not split the difference; do not charge the cholesterol because the ratio left nothing to charge.

**Boundary:** Settled disagreements run cholesterol above ratio: 323 against 5.3 (UW-T18) and 329 against 5.7 (UW-T20) were each charged the first-band 25, not the third-band 75; 263 against 3.9 (UW-T24) was charged nothing. A cholesterol of 321 or more can never agree with the ratio and is always charged on the ratio. The ratio above the cholesterol has no case: the ratio governs, charge its band, say judgement was used. The lipid line is one cardiac table for entries 13 and 14 when the ratio governs and charges, two when both charge (UW-T04 counted five with both in; UW-T20 counted four with the ratio alone), and none when the ratio governs to nothing (UW-T24) or both bands are zero (UW-T25 through UW-T27). A low HDL is never a factor of its own, and a high HDL is not a credit: it is already inside the ratio. A cholesterol above 240 with the ratio at zero still closes all three preferred classes by criterion on a zero-debit file (untested). The line resolves on its own and softens nothing else.

**Why:** UW-T18 charged 75 for cholesterol and 25 for the ratio and came out one step too severe; the reviewer: the ratio governs, the cholesterol band is not charged. UW-T20 applied the rule and the reviewer restated it while confirming 'lipid ratio' among the factors. UW-T24 applied it to nothing and the reviewer confirmed the five-factor list with no lipid line on it. The ratio already carries the HDL; a high total against a good HDL is priced by the ratio alone, and a good enough ratio prices it at zero.

## 16. Naming drivers

**When it applies:** Every file.

**What to do:** The drivers are the material factors the reviewer will list; build them the same way.

- One driver per table that carried a debit (or would have, on a postponed file), by factor not number, in the reviewer's words: 'build', 'blood pressure reading' (untreated), 'blood pressure treatment' (treated), 'total cholesterol' (only where charged, entry 15), 'lipid ratio' (only where charged, entry 15), 'A1c', 'family history' (only where charged, entry 12), 'occupation class' (class B or C), 'tobacco', 'sleep apnea', 'liver enzymes', 'moving violations', 'DUI'.
- One driver per modifier, sent or would-have-been-sent: 'aviation' for the flat extra (entry 6); the avocation's short name for a rider, 'climbing' or 'motorsport' (entry 5). The rider avocation is named though it carries no debit, and named on a postponed file though no rider is sent (UW-T24); the rider's detail carries the fuller wording ('technical rock climbing'). No avocation on the file means no avocation driver, whatever the occupation class (UW-T25).
- 'late-onset diabetes credit' beside 'A1c' where entry 10 credits, on a heavy file (UW-T10, UW-T17) and on a file where those two are the whole list (UW-T26). A credit that zeroes a line (entries 7, 8, 12) is not named, and neither is a cholesterol band the ratio overrode (263 on UW-T24).
- 'cardiac risk interaction' where entry 14 charges it (four or more cardiac tables), never for fewer.
- On a postponed file, the postponement reason plus every factor that would have rated (entry 3).
- Never a reading that carried no debit, a reading that only closed a higher preferred class, a credited-to-zero or dropped line, an overridden band, or an incidental detail: a hobby, a pet, a season ticket, bees, a guitar, crime novels, volunteering at a food bank, anything in the file's 'also on file' line, a stable weight, a normal build, a clean record or a single violation, tobacco never used or quit over five years, a negative nicotine screen, normal liver chemistry, an empty alcohol history, compliant apnea, no apnea, no family history, a class A occupation, no avocation, a low HDL with the ratio at zero, a high HDL, a figure that missed a preferred threshold inside its zero band, cover inside the multiple, cover in force, years on treatment, years since a diagnosis, days a year spent on an avocation, the applicant's age or sex or the product or the face amount.
- Zero tables charged, not postponed, no modifier: an empty list, whatever class the criteria reach (UW-T05 and UW-T27 at Preferred, UW-T07 at Standard Plus); the criteria that closed the higher classes belong in the rationale and never in the list. A file credited down to Standard under entry 10 is not zero tables charged: its list is 'A1c' and 'late-onset diabetes credit' (UW-T26).
- The order has not mattered: on UW-T23 and UW-T24 the lists matched the reviewer's in a different order; on UW-T25 and UW-T26 in the same order; all confirmed.

**Why:** The reviewer lists the material factors on every file and faults the drivers in every direction: too few (UW-T04), too many (UW-T05, UW-T10, UW-T18), wrong names (UW-T17). Seven on UW-T20 matched the reviewer's seven exactly while the class did not, and UW-T06's drivers matched on a file that should have been postponed: a right list is necessary, not sufficient. None on UW-T27 (the reviewer: the material factors were none), one on UW-T22 (blood pressure treatment), two on UW-T21 (tobacco, aviation) and UW-T26 (A1c, late-onset diabetes credit), three on UW-T25 (build, occupation class, moving violations), four on UW-T23 (build, occupation class, climbing, liver enzymes) and five on the postponed UW-T24 (DUI, occupation class, climbing, moving violations, liver enzymes) matched exactly on files the reviewer confirmed whole: the list is as long as the file, and nothing is added to make it look worked.

## 17. Cover inside the income multiple: one line, not a driver

**When it applies:** Face amount plus cover in force is at or under the multiple for the applicant's age.

**What to do:** State in one line that total cover sits inside the multiple (total, multiple, ceiling), run the DUI check (entry 2), and go on to the tables. Not a judgement item, not a driver, never a reason to postpone. In-force cover is always added in, however large or small beside the face applied for; nothing in force means the face amount alone is the total. Age 31 to 40 is 25x; 41 to 50 is 20x; 51 to 60 is 15x, age 60 included; 61 and over is 10x.

**Why:** Every file other than UW-T02 has been inside the multiple and no financial question arose (UW-T27: $750,000 plus $150,000 in force, $900,000 against a 20x ceiling of $5,200,000 at 48; UW-T26: $250,000 with nothing in force against a 15x ceiling of $3,150,000 at 56; UW-T25: $650,000 against a 25x ceiling of $4,375,000 at 38; UW-T24: $900,000 against a 25x ceiling of $2,125,000 at 35; UW-T23: $600,000 against a 15x ceiling of $1,275,000 at 54; UW-T22: $500,000 against a 25x ceiling of $2,125,000 at 40; UW-T21: $250,000 against a 15x ceiling of $2.1M at 57; UW-T20: $900,000 against a 10x ceiling of $1.75M at 63; UW-T13: $600,000 against $1.75M at 65; UW-T19: $1,000,000 against $1.7M at 49). UW-T06, UW-T09 and UW-T24 were postponed on the DUI instead, which is why the two postponement checks run independently and both are always written down.

## 18. Zero-debit file: read the preferred class off its criteria, and the drivers are none

**When it applies:** Every table reads zero, outright or because a referred item was credited to zero, dropped or overridden to zero; neither postponement check trips; no modifier. Settled three times: UW-T05 (Preferred), UW-T07 (Standard Plus) and UW-T27 (Preferred).

**What to do:** Decision `accept`. Work the three preferred classes from the top, every criterion of each against the file. One criterion missed closes that class, however clean the rest; zero debits meeting none is Standard. State the class reached and which criteria closed the classes above it, in the rationale. Drivers empty; modifiers empty.

**Points that have decided cases:** Blood pressure is two criteria, systolic and diastolic each against its own limit: on UW-T07 a systolic of 124 met every class and a diastolic of 86 closed Preferred Plus and Preferred, so Standard Plus was the answer; on UW-T27, 124/75 met all three. Lipids are two criteria of one class, read on the printed cholesterol and ratio, both to be met: cholesterol 211 and ratio 4.1 each miss Preferred Plus (200 and 4.0) and both meet Preferred (220 and 4.5) (UW-T27); a cholesterol of 215 likewise meets Preferred but not Preferred Plus. A1c is read against 5.6, 6.0 and 6.4: 5.9 closes Preferred Plus and meets Preferred (UW-T27), as does 6.0. Tobacco never used meets every class; quit over five years meets Preferred and Standard Plus, never Preferred Plus. A clean record with no DUI on the file meets '0 moving violations and no DUI ever'. Class A with no avocation meets every class, and an unlisted pastime (first-edition crime novels, UW-T27) is not an avocation. No family events, no apnea, no alcohol history and normal liver chemistry meet every class; a stable BMI of 23.8 meets every class. Age, sex, product and face amount play no part. The rationale shape confirmed on UW-T27: one line placing cover inside the multiple with no DUI; one line that nothing is referred; one line that every table reads zero and no cardiac table charges; one line that the incidental detail is not an avocation; the criteria that close Preferred Plus named; the statement that every Preferred criterion is met; accept at Preferred, no modifier, drivers none.

**Written but untested:** a single violation leaves a zero-debit file at Standard; any diabetes or apnea diagnosis and any credited liver rise close all three; a family event dropped for age counts against the family criteria (entry 12); build is read on the adjusted weight; a cholesterol above 240 whose band the ratio overrode still closes all three.

**Boundary:** Only for a total of zero with no modifier. Any debit closes all three preferred classes; do not work or name the criteria on a charged file, one clause that the charges close them is enough (UW-T22, UW-T23, UW-T25, UW-T26). A file whose only charge is an A1c credited one band under entry 10 is not this entry: it reads Standard through entry 21 on the credited total, its drivers are 'A1c' and 'late-onset diabetes credit', and the diagnosis closes the preferred classes without the criteria being worked (UW-T26). A zero-debit pilot is not this entry either: the flat extra makes the file entry 6 and entry 21, and the hazardous avocation closes every preferred class, so the answer is Standard with the modifier (untested). 'Standard' is therefore reached three ways: here by criteria with an empty list; under entry 21 as the 0-49 band of a charged total; and under entry 21 as a Table 2 total credited one band; the name is the same and the drivers differ.

**Why:** UW-T05 (Preferred, material factors none; naming the closing criteria as drivers was the one error), UW-T07 (Standard Plus, empty list, confirmed) and UW-T27 (male 48, whole life $750,000 with $150,000 in force; BMI 23.8 stable, never tobacco with a negative screen, 124/75 untreated, cholesterol 211 with ratio 4.1, A1c 5.9 with no diagnosis, no family events, schoolteacher, no avocation, clean record, normal liver chemistry, no apnea, crime novels on the side; Preferred, accept, empty list; the reviewer: correct, the material factors were none). The class on a clean file is decided by the criteria; the drivers record only charges, credits against the total, modifiers and decision-forcing facts, and on a clean file there are none.

## 19. Nothing on the file is referred: say so in one line and rate

**When it applies:** Nothing on the file touches a referral line. The lines and where each is settled: recent change in build (entry 9, a loss); treated blood pressure (entry 11, any treated file); lipid bands that disagree (entry 15, including a charged cholesterol against a zero ratio); late-onset metabolic disease (entry 10, needs a diagnosis and a charged A1c); family history past the qualifying age (entry 12, needs an event and an applicant over 60); private aviation (entry 6); hazardous occupation with hazardous avocation (entry 5, needs both); recent motoring conviction (entry 2, the DUI line); borderline liver chemistry (entry 8, below twice normal); treated sleep-disordered breathing (entry 7, CPAP in use); face amount large relative to income (entry 1); combination of cardiac risk factors (entries 13 and 14, needs at least one charged cardiac table, and adds nothing below four).

**What to do:** Write one sentence that no line is referred, then rate on the tables and, if every table is zero, on the preferred criteria (entry 18). Do not manufacture a judgement item: a stable weight in a charged band, an A1c with no diagnosis, no family events, one moving violation, two or three moving violations, enzymes at or above twice normal, apnea with no CPAP, tobacco quit within five years, tobacco quit over five years with a negative screen, a class B or C occupation with no avocation, a low HDL with the ratio at zero, readings that miss a preferred threshold inside their zero band, cover inside the multiple and an unlisted pastime are none of them referrals. Age, sex and product are never factors.

**Boundary:** A charged file can have nothing referred: UW-T25 (stable BMI 30.1, class C lineman with no avocation, two violations, guitar on the side) had three charged tables and not one referral line live, and was rated on the tables at Table 4 and confirmed whole. A clean file never has anything referred: UW-T27 (every table zero, crime novels on the side) said so in one line, went to the criteria and was confirmed at Preferred. Where referral lines are live, dispose of each under its entry with one sentence, apply this entry to every other line, and do not go looking for more: UW-T20 had three live lines (lipid bands, family history for age, the cardiac combination at four tables); UW-T21 one (private aviation); UW-T22 one (treated blood pressure); UW-T23 one (class C with technical climbing); UW-T24 three (a one-year-old DUI, class C with climbing, a first-band cholesterol against a zero-band ratio); UW-T26 one (type 2 diabetes diagnosed at about 49); on each, everything else was charged as written or left at zero, and the reviewer confirmed all of them whole.

**Why:** UW-T05, UW-T07, UW-T11, UW-T15, UW-T16, UW-T19, UW-T25 and UW-T27 had nothing referred, said so in one sentence, were rated on the tables and were confirmed. Judgement is spent where the manual asks for it and nowhere else.

## 20. Tobacco quit within five years: charge as written, name 'tobacco', the negative screen changes nothing

**When it applies:** Declared tobacco use that stopped between one and five years ago.

**What to do:** Charge the section 7 debit and name 'tobacco'. A negative nicotine screen confirms the declaration and nothing more: not a credit, not a driver, not a judgement item. The debit closes all three preferred classes; the file goes to entry 21. Where it is the only charge the total reads Standard (UW-T16 alone; UW-T21 with an aviation flat extra beside it, which changes the decision to accept with modification and nothing about the class).

**Boundary:** Never used is zero and unnamed, meets the tobacco criterion of every preferred class, and a negative screen beside it is unmentioned (UW-T22, UW-T23, UW-T25, UW-T27). Quit over five years is a non-smoker at zero, unnamed, eligible for Preferred and Standard Plus but never Preferred Plus, and a negative screen beside it is likewise unmentioned (UW-T24, UW-T26). Current use, or a nicotine-positive result against a declared never, is governed by the manual's smoker rule (add the smoker debit, cap the best class at Standard); untested, rate as the manual writes and say so. Tobacco is not a cardiac table.

**Why:** Named by the reviewer on every file with a quit-within-five-years declaration: UW-T02, UW-T08, UW-T10, UW-T11, UW-T16, UW-T18, UW-T20 and UW-T21, the screen negative and unmentioned each time it was on the file.

## 21. A file with table debits: accept at the class the total reads; a flat extra or rider makes it accept with modification

**When it applies:** At least one table charges after the referred items are resolved under entries 5 to 15; no single table is in a decline band; neither postponement check trips. A file that trips a postponement check is entry 2 or 1 however its tables would have read (UW-T24 carried three charged tables and a would-be rider, and was postponed).

**What to do:** Add every table debit as entries 7 to 12 and 15 leave the readings, add the entry 14 interaction where four or more cardiac tables charge, take any entry 10 credit, and read the class off the section 2 bands, lower edges included: 25 is Standard (UW-T03, UW-T12, UW-T16, UW-T22; UW-T21 with an aviation flat extra beside it); 50 credited one band under entry 10 is Standard (UW-T26); 50 and 75 uncredited are Table 2 (UW-T15; UW-T13, UW-T19); 100 is Table 4 (UW-T18; UW-T25 plain; UW-T23 with a climbing rider beside it); 150 is Table 6 (UW-T14); 175 with the interaction on top is Table 8 (UW-T20); 200 credited under entry 10 is Table 6 (UW-T10, UW-T17). With no modifier the decision is `accept` and modifiers are empty. With an aviation flat extra (entry 6) or an exclusion rider (entry 5) the decision is `accept_with_modification`, the modifier is sent with its band or its named hazard, and the class is still the one the total reads, Standard and Table 4 both seen. Drivers under entry 16. Do not soften because the applicant is otherwise clean, do not add because the file feels heavy beyond what entry 14 charges, do not postpone for evidence the tables do not ask for. The product changes nothing (term and whole life have both been confirmed at Standard and at Table 4). A rationale shape the reviewer has confirmed: one line placing cover inside the multiple and noting no DUI, or the postponement and its reasons; one line per referred item and how its entry resolved it, or one line that nothing is referred; one line per charged table naming the factor, and one line saying the other tables are zero and any incidental detail is not an avocation; one line counting the cardiac tables and stating any interaction charged, or that none charge; any credit taken and the band it moved; the class the total reads and a clause that the charge or the diagnosis closes the preferred classes, or rating class null; the decision and any modifier.

**Boundary:** A total in the decline band or a single table reading decline is `decline` under the manual; untested, and flying or climbing alone can never produce it. Every table zero with no modifier is entry 18; a charged total credited down into the 0-49 band is still this entry, with the charged table and the credit as drivers (UW-T26).

**Why:** Every rated file has been confirmed at the class read off a correctly built total, and each correction has named the building step that was missed: a referred item charged raw (UW-T01, UW-T10, UW-T18), a credit withheld at a boundary (UW-T17), the interaction charge omitted at four cardiac tables (UW-T20), a postponement missed (UW-T02, UW-T06), or a wrong drivers list (UW-T04, UW-T05, UW-T10, UW-T17, UW-T18). The settled shapes: UW-T21 (tobacco 25, aviation flat extra, Standard, accept with modification, two drivers) a light file carrying a modifier; UW-T22 (blood pressure treatment 25, Standard, accept, one driver) a light file carrying a single referred charge; UW-T26 (A1c 50 credited one band, Standard, accept, two drivers) a light file carrying a single credited charge; UW-T23 (occupation class 50, build 25, liver enzymes 25, climbing rider, Table 4, accept with modification, four drivers) a mid-weight file carrying a rider; UW-T25 (occupation class 50, build 25, moving violations 25, Table 4, accept, three drivers, nothing referred) a mid-weight file with nothing to resolve but the tables; UW-T24 (recent DUI, occupation class, climbing, moving violations, liver enzymes, postponed, five drivers) a rateable file that a recent DUI takes off the table; and, under entry 18 rather than here, UW-T27 (nothing charged, nothing referred, Preferred by criteria, accept, no drivers) a clean file. All seven were confirmed whole.
